$comment: Which locales exist, and which of them SHIP -- decision D1-14.
The `shipped` flag is what makes i18n-lint's missing-key rule able to fail at all. With every
locale unshipped the rule would be vacuous; with every locale shipped, zh_CN and ja would fail
from the day they were declared. Declaring them as not-yet-shipped makes their absence DATA THE
GATE READS rather than a case nobody wrote -- which is the whole difference between a planned
gap and a forgotten one. `i18n-lint --explain` lists them with the reason, so a silent skip
cannot be mistaken for a locale someone forgot.
THE KEY IS THE SOURCE STRING. Every locale, `en` included, is a real catalog: the sources hold
catalog keys (core/Result.h forbids user-facing English in core/, and ActionId.def carries one
`action.*` key per action), so there is no English in the code for lupdate to extract and no
identity locale. A missing key in `en` is therefore a detectable defect rather than an invisible
fallback that renders `action.file.open` on a button.
